title: 2000 AMC 10 Problem 20
statement: Let \(A,\) \(M,\) and \(C\) be nonnegative integers such that \(A + M + C = 10.\) What is the maximum value of \[ \begin{aligned} &A \cdot M \cdot C + A \cdot M \\ &\quad {}+ M \cdot C + C \cdot A? \end{aligned} \]

solutions.text:
Notice that \[ \begin{gathered} A \cdot M \cdot C + AM + MC + CA \\ = (A+1)(M+1)(C+1) \\ {}- (A + M + C) - 1 \\ = (A+1)(M+1)(C+1) - 11. \end{gathered} \]

We maximize a product of three positive integers summing to \(13.\) The most balanced split is \(4, 4, 5,\) giving \(4 \cdot 4 \cdot 5 = 80.\)

The maximum is \(80 - 11 = 69.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Add \(1\) to each variable and expand \((A+1)(M+1)(C+1)\)
The expression equals \((A+1)(M+1)(C+1) - 11,\) so maximize a product of three positive integers summing to \(13\)
